contents.name: Unitary equivalence of separable Hilbert spaces
Cardinality of orthonormal bases
contents.reason: Equality of arbitrary basis cardinalities is not used by the given-basis coordinate isometry or the supplied-sequence separable classification; its full proof has not been certified here.

contents.name: Almost periodic functions example
contents.reason: This constructs an additional almost-periodic completion and Bohr inner product, beyond the compact finite-dimensional tori and Hilbert coordinate models assigned to this pair.

contents.name: Gram determinant
contents.reason: Finite Gram determinant computations belong with the preceding geometry and Gram–Schmidt examples; no determinant formula is required by this page.

contents.name: Matrix coefficients against a fixed orthonormal basis
Closed bounded set without a norm minimizer
contents.reason: The distinction between arbitrary closed sets and closed convex sets belongs to the preceding projection geometry companion.

contents.name: Dirichlet kernel representation
contents.reason: Kernel estimates for pointwise partial sums require a separate convergence theory; no pointwise convergence follows from the present L2 theorem.

contents.name: Riemann–Lebesgue lemma
contents.reason: Decay of all L1 coefficients is useful in the later pointwise Fourier development; the current Hilbert Bessel estimate covers only L2 and is not substituted for it.

contents.name: Smoothness and summability; lacunary continuous non-AC example
contents.reason: Coefficient smoothness estimates and the lacunary failure of absolute continuity need their own function-space hypotheses and are retained for the lacunary page.

contents.name: Fejer kernel and uniform Fejer convergence
contents.reason: Cesaro uniform summability is distinct from ordinary L2 partial-sum convergence; the selected basis proof instead follows the assigned Stone–Weierstrass route.

contents.name: Dini pointwise convergence
contents.reason: The integrable difference-quotient hypothesis is pointwise convergence machinery and must not be silently attached to arbitrary L2 classes.

contents.name: Dirichlet–Dini criterion
contents.reason: One-sided regularity and endpoint values are necessary for this result; the two waveform examples here make only norm convergence assertions.

contents.name: Dirichlet and Fejer kernel formulas
contents.reason: Exact summability kernel formulas belong to the later kernel-based theory and are not needed for the algebraic density route.

contents.name: Completely continuous noncompact identity on ell1
contents.reason: The Schur-property witness separates sequential weak behavior from compactness and belongs with the upstream Schur theorem.

contents.name: Reflexive converse for completely continuous maps
contents.reason: The converse requires the earlier reflexive weak-subsequence theorem; the assigned compact-map theorem preserves only its universally valid forward direction.

contents.name: AP equivalence with all-domain compact approximation
contents.reason: The converse is a substantive AP characterization and the source only poses it as an exercise; its full proof must be supplied upstream before extending the present forward AP remark.

contents.name: Schauder basis implies approximation property
contents.reason: The existing upstream inventory owns the stronger bounded approximation property consequence of a Schauder basis.

contents.name: Calkin algebra reformulation
contents.reason: The quotient Banach algebra is defined only at FA-17; parametrix Atkinson is already stated without that future structure.

contents.name: Contour representation of spectral projection
contents.reason: The contour integral requires later holomorphic functional calculus; only the stabilized direct-sum projection is used at this stage.

contents.name: Argyros–Haydon scalar-plus-compact example
contents.reason: The scalar-plus-compact construction is a deep additional Banach-space pathology and is not a supplier for general Riesz–Schauder theory; its construction is not verified in this dispatch.
